articles.title: Super Bowl-winning coach Bruce Arians partners urges prostate cancer screenings: 'It will save your life'
articles.summary: Bruce Arians shared his prostate cancer survival story during the NFL's "Crucial Catch" week, urging men to get a simple PSA blood test every year.
articles.body: This week, the NFL continues its "Crucial Catch" initiative, an annual partnership with the American Cancer Society focused on fighting cancer through early detection, risk reduction and screening awareness. For former Super Bowl-winning head coach Bruce Arians, it’s the perfect time to share his prostate cancer survival story, and more importantly, stress how simple it is to get screened today. Arians partnered with Novartis for it’s "Relax, It’s a Blood Test" campaign to raise awareness about prostate cancer screening and the importance of early detection. It was a no-brainer because, in 2007, early detection helped his doctors find the prostate cancer he was diagnosed with and remove it. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "Being Crucial Catch just being kicked off this week in the NFL, it’s a great partnership. Getting the message out to all men about early detection. One in eight men in the United States are going to have prostate cancer, and early detection is the key. It’s a simple finger-free blood test," Arians told OutKick in a recent interview. Arians admitted the moment he heard his diagnosis, it was "devastating." But if it wasn’t for his PSA, or prostate-specific antigen, blood test, perhaps things could’ve been much worse. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "I thought I was just like every other man going to the bathroom too much at night. I had started my scorecard at 40, and when I say start a scorecard, get your PSA level checked every year by your doctor. Know your risk and get screened," Arians said. "For me, I went in, got the diagnosis. Doctor said, ‘You know, let’s just do a biopsy just in case.’ Fortunately, we found the prostate cancer and had it removed. I was 51 and had all those anxieties that all men have for what’s to come. But the doctors, they have such a great way of saving the nerves and everything else. And you want that cancer out of your body. For me, it was very easy. Just went to work the next 10 days with a catheter and got ready for the draft. "I was very, very fortunate to have a fantastic doctor, and the personal part of it is why I’m so involved with Novartis and the campaign." It’s a serious initiative by Novartis, but Arians did have a bit of fun with some play-on football worlds. In the campaign, he urges athletes to "relax their tight ends," emphasizing how prostate cancer screenings can begin with the PSA test rather than a rectal exam. Legendary tight ends Rob Gronkowski and Tony Gonzalez were involved with the campaign as well. The truth is, if detected early, the five-year relative survival rate of prostate cancer is over 99%, making screenings super important for men. Get your PSA level checked every single year and stay in tune with your doctor. If you’re not one of those guys that goes to the doctor very often, this is the one you need to go to. It will save your life." SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

articles.title: “We are proud to continue to support”: How Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ $25,000 foundation move backed college scholarships for Navy SEAL children
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have used their 15 and the Mahomies Foundation to support children in different ways. On Nov.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have used their 15 and the Mahomies Foundation to support children in different ways. On Nov. 11, 2022, the foundation turned its attention to families connected to the U.S. Navy SEALs. It gave the SEAL Legacy Foundation a $25,000 grant to support college scholarships for children of SEALs who made the ultimate sacrifice.The donation went beyond a single scholarship. It supported the Honored SEAL Legacy Scholarship Program, which helps children of fallen Navy SEALs cover college costs. The program honors more than 100 SEALs who have died since 9/11.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes foundation backed a $25,000 scholarship fund for Navy SEAL childrenThe 15 and the Mahomies Foundation announced the $25,000 grant on Veterans Day, Nov. 11, 2022. The money went to the SEAL Legacy Foundation for its Honored SEAL Legacy Scholarship Program, which awards annual college scholarships for academic and related costs to children of U.S. Navy SEALs.The program carries the names of SEALs who lost their lives since the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks. According to the SEAL Legacy Foundation, each scholarship now carries a $5,000 award and can support tuition, vocational programs, and associate or bachelor’s degree programs.For Patrick, the project also carried a message about remembering the families left behind.“We are proud to continue to support the children of U.S. Navy SEALs through the Honored SEAL Legacy Foundation Scholarship Program,” Mahomes said in the foundation’s Veterans Day announcement on Nov. 11, 2022. “Honoring the work and sacrifice of the SEALs, and providing resources for their families is a core focus of the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation.”That focus fits the foundation’s wider work with children and young people. Founded by Mahomes in 2019, 15 and the Mahomies supports programs tied to health, wellness, education and communities that need resources. Its charitable partners also include organizations such as the SEAL Legacy Foundation, Make-A-Wish, Special Olympics Missouri and Boys & Girls Clubs.The scholarship program has supported families of more than 100 fallen SEALsThe 2022 grant was not the foundation’s first connection with the SEAL Legacy Foundation.On May 25, 2020, 15 and the Mahomies announced funding for 15 scholarships through the same Honored SEAL Legacy Scholarship Program. At the time, the foundation said the scholarships would support families of more than 100 Navy SEALs who had died since 9/11.Mahomes also spoke about the foundation’s commitment in that May 25, 2020 announcement, saying, “no one will be left behind.” He made the comment while announcing the 15 scholarships for children of U.S. Navy SEALs through the SEAL Legacy Foundation.The program continues to serve SEAL families. The SEAL Legacy Foundation says its scholarship supports children of active-duty, retired, separated or reserve Navy SEALs. Each $5,000 award can help with tuition and other education costs.For Mahomes and the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation, the $25,000 grant showed another side of their charitable work. Instead of focusing on football or athletic programs, the foundation helped families connected to military service and put education at the center of its support.That makes the 2022 Veterans Day contribution a notable part of the Mahomes foundation’s work, especially because the scholarship program continues to honor the children and families of SEALs who never came home.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tyreek Hill's wife testifies about alleged assault, verbal abuse at trial ahead of his potential NFL return
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill is gearing up to sign with an NFL team after a serious knee injury knocked him out early last season.
articles.body:
Content Warning: This story contains depictions of alleged domestic violence.

Tyreek Hill's wife detailed the verbal abuse and assaults she suffered throughout their relationship during testimony in the first day of a civil assault-and-battery trial in Florida on Tuesday.

The testimony came just one day after Hill's agent told ESPN that the former star wide receiver could sign with a team in the coming days, potentially even a reunion with the Kansas City Chiefs.

Lakeeta Vaccaro testified during the trial Tuesday, which is part of the couple's divorce proceedings, according to ESPN's Michael Rothstein . Vaccaro, who is the sister of former New Orleans Saints and Tennessee Titans safety Kenny Vaccaro, said that the alleged abuse started in January 2024 when the two were arguing over a post-nuptial agreement Hill was pressuring her to sign. She didn't sign, and said she disagreed with stipulations in the document. Hill then threatened divorce, tried to take her wedding ring off, grabbed a necklace off of her neck, put his hands around her neck, grabbed and twisted her breasts and wrestled her to the bed, she testified. The incident, she said, "terrified" her.

Several other instances of alleged abuse were brought up during the court proceedings on Tuesday. Once, in July 2024, Vaccaro said that Hill attacked her while she was pregnant and tried to punch her in the stomach, which she blocked. In January 2024, while they were on a trip to Orlando, she said that Hill told her that he was going to cheat on her and wanted a divorce. When he came back to their hotel room the next morning, she said he threw her clothes out of a suitcase, broke her computer, took her wedding ring off and twisted one of her breasts. Police were called, but charges were not filed.

Later that month, after an argument about the post-nuptial agreement, Vaccaro said that Hill threw her luggage out of the house, and then Hill physically threw her out. She said that he "ended up throwing or shoving" an unlit cigar butt in her mouth. Police were called then, too.

Vaccaro said that Hill kicked her out of their car while they were driving home from an event in May 2024, and that he threw her shoe out of the car. In November 2024, Vaccaro said that Hill yelled at her and spit in her face after she didn't have a pregame outfit ready for him. She went into labor the next day with their child.

In April 2025, Vaccaro said that Hill punched her computer, threw it to the ground and cursed at her. The argument ended up spilling over into their daughter's room while she was asleep.

"I've been in this cycle with him for so long, being pregnant and realizing, what am I going to do? How am I going to get myself out of this," Vaccaro testified Tuesday, via ESPN. "[The abuse] got worse and worse and worse. And it got to a point where, now I'm a new mom. I have to think of her. I have to think about what I'm putting myself through."

Hill, 31, is working his way back from a serious knee injury that he suffered last season with the Miami Dolphins. His leg was left pointing in the wrong direction, and he was diagnosed with a dislocated kneecap and multiple torn ligaments. The Dolphins released him in February, and he's been a free agent recovering ever since.

Hill previously played six seasons with the Chiefs, and helped them win Super Bowl LIV. The team lost Rashee Rice (hamstring injury) and Tyquan Thornton (dislocated ankle) in the team's win over the Raiders on Sunday .

It's unclear if Hill will face discipline for his alleged abuse from the league if he signs with the Chiefs or elsewhere. The allegations, NFL spokesperson Brian McCarthy told ESPN, remain "under review of the personal conduct policy."

articles.title: Tom Brady and Gisele Bundchen faced an unexpected $1,000,000 lawsuit weeks after their wedding over a shocking Costa Rica incident
articles.summary: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen had only been married for weeks when their Costa Rica wedding celebrations turned into a legal fight. In Sept.
articles.body: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen had only been married for weeks when their Costa Rica wedding celebrations turned into a legal fight. In Sept. 2009, two photographers and Agence France-Presse sued the former couple for at least $1 million. They accused security guards linked to the couple of confronting them and firing at their car after they took pictures near the property.The case drew attention because it involved Tom Brady, Gisele Bündchen, their wedding celebrations and an alleged shooting. But the lawsuit never went to trial in New York. On May 26, 2010, Judge Judith Gische dismissed the case, saying New York did not have jurisdiction over the couple.Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen faced $1 million claims after the Costa Rica incidentThe dispute began during an April 2009 celebration at Gisele Bündchen’s holiday home in Costa Rica. Photographer Yuri Cortez, who worked for Agence France-Presse, and Rolando Aviles of Costa Rican newspaper Al Dia went to cover the couple.The photographers claimed that security guards approached them and demanded their cameras and memory cards. According to their lawsuit, they refused and headed back to their vehicle. They then alleged that security guards fired at the car, damaging its rear windshield.Cortez, Aviles and Agence France-Presse sought at least $1 million in damages when they filed the lawsuit in September 2009. Their complaint also accused Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen of responsibility for the actions of the security team.Brady strongly denied the shooting allegation.In a 2009 interview with Sports Illustrated, while discussing the Costa Rica incident, Brady called the photographers' claims “absolute total b.s.” He also said, “Our security guys didn't even have guns. There were no shots fired.”That gave the case two sharply different accounts. The photographers described a frightening confrontation, while Brady denied that anyone fired a weapon.The legal fight then moved to the question of where the case belonged. The photographers filed in New York, but Judge Judith Gische dismissed the case on May 26, 2010. She said Brady and Bündchen lived in Massachusetts and that the alleged incident happened in Costa Rica.Gische also dismissed the claims against Gisele Bündchen, finding no evidence that she had been involved in hiring or directing the security guards. The ruling did not determine whether the photographers' allegations were true. It only meant the New York court would not hear the case.The Costa Rican legal proceedings involving the security guards continued separately.Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen later faced FTX investor lawsuitMore than a decade later, Brady and Bündchen found themselves connected to another high-profile lawsuit, this time over cryptocurrency exchange FTX.After FTX collapsed in Nov. 2022, investors sued several celebrities who promoted the company, including Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen. The plaintiffs argued that celebrity endorsements helped attract customers and alleged violations tied to FTX's business and securities offerings.The case later narrowed. In May 2025, a federal judge dismissed many claims against the celebrity defendants but allowed some claims under Florida and Oklahoma law to continue, according to Reuters.The FTX case differs sharply from the 2009 wedding lawsuit. The earlier case centered on allegations involving security guards at the couple's Costa Rica property, while the later litigation focused on Brady and Bündchen's promotional relationship with FTX.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jermaine Eluemunor: British New York Giants star reveals rise from rock bottom to NFL success story two decades after discovering football in London
articles.summary: Britain's Jermaine Eluemunor opens up on his battle with mental health and inspiring the next generation with his journey to NFL stardom; This story covers themes of mental health, which some may find distressing. If you are affected by this story, please visit sky.com/viewersupport
articles.body:
The Giants offensive tackle dresses up, hosts pretend tea parties and plays the role of punching bag as a proud girl-dad to his young daughters of a week day, and manhandles the greatest athletes on the planet of a weekend. He enjoys the serenity of fishing and escapism of anime off the field, and flourishes in the art of violence on it.

Eluemunor has bridged a transatlantic chasm, swatted away early rejection and overcome 'rock bottom' amid the fiercest of challenges to his mental health to emerge as one of Britain's most gifted footballing exports and, so too, one of the NFL's premier players in his position.

Life wasn't always going to be this way. He now hopes his story can prescribe immunity to the notion of impossible.

"I grew up in Chalk Farm, North West London, right next to Camden Town," Eluemunor tells Sky Sports. "I grew up in a flat on Ferdinand Street, quite small actually, I was just thinking about how small those places were. I went back to see it and I don't even think I fit through the front door now."

It was around this time in 2007 when Eluemunor first discovered football, a session of channel-flicking on TV seeing him stumble across the first-ever NFL regular-season game to be played in London as the Giants faced the Miami Dolphins at Wembley Stadium. Almost two decades on, he is starting for the team where it all began, for whom his impact was rewarded with a $39m contract extension this past offseason and a role as captain this past weekend.

"It was just spur of the moment luck, honestly," he says. "I think that God intended for me to find that game because he knew that was part of my purpose in life to play this game at the highest level and try to achieve what I'm attempting to achieve."

Eluemunor, now 31, moved to New Jersey with his father at the age of 14 in search of greater opportunities, before first playing American football at Morris Knolls High School. His dwarfing stature made an immediate impression, while also prompting some early book-cover-judgement from one coach who made the assumption of a ready-made monster.

"I had never touched a weight in my entire life," he says. "I remember them putting 225 up on the bar and I lifted it up and it fell right on my chest because I wasn't strong at all. Now I can bench over 500 pounds. It was a crazy first day for me, and then just walking around, I'm the English kid."

Despite spending half of his life stateside, he will seemingly forever remain the 'British guy' of NFL locker rooms.

"People still make fun of me for being British every single day, that's never going to go away," he jokes. "I'm literally made fun of for being English every single day, people do English accents every single day."

Still, Eluemunor has never been one to shirk his roots, and this year returned to the UK to stage a four-day camp series that would reach 385 kids. The family of one child notably drove more than two hours each way to attend one of the sessions.

"It's about showing kids that it doesn't matter where you live, where you're from, the colour of your skin, tall, short, big, small, it doesn't matter who you are, you can achieve whatever you want in life," he explained. "I try to be a figure that they can look to as inspiration because I wasn't anything growing up.

"I had dreams, but I didn't know if they were possible to achieve. I want to show these kids that you may not be where you want to be right now, but if you keep working, there's nothing stopping you from achieving what you want to achieve."

His tale is one of patience and persistence. Eluemunor, despite the hundreds of emails he sent to schools across the country, was not initially recruited by any college programs out of high school and as a result joined Lackawanna College. Such was his impact on the football field he was eventually recruited by 35 colleges and spent three years with Texas A&M before being selected by the Baltimore Ravens in the fifth round of the 2017 NFL Draft. The transition, as it had been upon arriving in the US, would prove anything but an easy weight to shift.

He made just three starts in his first two seasons with the Ravens, remembering vividly of the fans that had claimed he 'sucked' while suggesting he did not belong in the NFL. Eluemunor was ultimately traded to the New England Patriots in August 2019, prompting the most difficult and yet most defining chapter of his career.

"It shaped me completely," he says. "I was the lowest of the lowest in New England, it was pretty tough, really tough.

"I learned a lot about myself. I learned a lot about what it took to really belong in this league. But then also I learned that mentally, I'm a lot stronger than I think I am. If I can get through that, I can get through anything."

Eluemunor was limited to 29 snaps on offense in his first campaign in New England, his progress hindered by an ankle injury in Week Six before a Patriots teammate fell on his leg upon his return to practice, leaving him in tears amid another setback to his career.

He admits he became guilty of buying into criticism he read on social media and in turn speaking negatively about himself, at one stage crying to Patriots trainer Daryl Nelson amid his troubled efforts to transition to a new role at left tackle.

"Everyone has a goal and a dream, and when you feel that thing slip away and you feel there's nothing you can do to control that, you kind of just go into a spiral. And before you know, you can hit rock bottom," he explains.

"In order to get out of rock bottom, it takes certain people to pull you from that, you can't do it alone. You need people to help you along the way. I had great people in my life that truly helped pull me out from rock bottom and put me on the path that I needed to be on.

"I'm a very lucky person because not a lot of people can get all the way to rock bottom and be able to pull themselves out and make something of themselves. I'm a lucky person, but I also work really, really hard, I worked really hard to get away from that mentally and I worked really hard to get where I'm at now."

At his lowest, he would have to field questions as to whether he ever thought about taking his own life, previously insisting he never quite strayed as far as that idea, largely thanks to a devoted support network led by his wife Christina.

"I think that nowadays mental health is such a huge thing, I think the more people are willing to be open about it, the better things will be," he explains.

"A lot of the times we think that we have to be these strong, tough, imposing figures, especially being an offensive lineman in the NFL, people start to think of you as superhero-esque and they don't think that you're a normal person.

"But to be able to share the way you feel and what you're going through and show just how normal you really are, I think that goes a long way in shedding light on subjects that are a little bit more sensitive, especially when it comes to mental health.

"If you can learn how to control the narrative and just work hard and really be vulnerable and open with people, then you'll see that people are way more accepting than you think and believe. Then you find a great group or team like I've been lucky enough to find with the Giants, then people just fall in love with you and the person you are and you don't have to be someone you're not and you're able to just be yourself."

Eluemunor became a free agent following the 2020 season before being cut by both the Miami Dolphins and Jacksonville Jaguars during preseason. He then signed with the Las Vegas Raiders and made three starts at right guard before being benched for the remainder of the season.

He was handed a one-year $1.3m deal to stay with the team in 2022, paving the way for his most productive year yet as Eluemunor started all 17 games to earn a $3m extension. Criticism of his work ethic and attitude from interim coach Rich Bisaccia had ignited a dogged reply; the physical attributes to dominate and the potential to cement a starting spot in the NFL had always been there to be unlocked, and everybody knew it. Coaches were desperate to see Eluemunor fulfil as much, and put on a smile while doing so.

Still, for all his progress, Eluemunor remained conscious to his struggles in New England and the lingering threat of slipping back into the same headspace. He was put in contact with mental health coach Brian Cain, who later made Eluemunor a "mental movie" that he could watch before playing, depicting images of his loved ones along with some of his best moments on the field.

"I watch it before every game because it kind of puts perspective into place and shows me why I do what I do and what I need to do to go out there and be successful. he's been a huge person for me," he says.

"I have my baby girls and I do this for my wife, that's my reason, that's my why. I want them to go back and look at my career and be like, you know, our dad did this for us and he was one of the best players, if not the best player in his position when we were kids.

"I want them to be like, he did everything, accomplished everything he wanted to accomplish, so there's no reason why we can't accomplish what we want to accomplish."

It is the same message he continues to relay to the children he meets during camps such as the one this past summer in the UK.

"Mental health is such a sensitive subject, especially with the younger generation, that you have to be able to be vulnerable and show them who you truly are," he continues. "When I put the face mask on, I'm still the same person. And I want to show them that, just because I'm a professional athlete and make all this money, it doesn't mean I'm different from any of you.

"I try to show them every single day that we're not too far apart and we're not any different than each other. It's the person you are deep within you who makes you who you are."

The Jermaine Eluemunor of today will tell you he is the best right tackle in the NFL. Of that much he holds zero doubts.

He will publicly welcome the prospect of being left one-on-one on an island against the TJ Watts of the world, eager to test himself against the best and equally convinced that he will come out on top. As of Week Four this season, no offensive tackle has been left on an 'island' at a higher rate than Eluemunor's 71.4 per cent, according to Pro Football Focus; what's more, he has won those battles 93.7 per cent of the time.

"I've grown a lot mentally," he says. "I can look back at that kid in New England and say that I'm a million times the player I was mentally and physically.

"You have to go through things like that in order to get to where you want to get to and become the person you want to become. I believe that was a trial that I put in my life and to see if I was going to make it through to truly become who I want to become.

"I've always been driven to be the best. I just didn't do the work that was required to be the best."

Eluemunor signed a two-year deal with the Giants back in March 2024 and has since established himself as an instrumental piece to his team's offensive line. It has taken countless trials and obstacles to get here, but there is now a sense of long-awaited stability and momentum capable of inciting the best version of the man from Chalk Farm, London.

"I've had a lot of ups and downs, prior to me getting to New York there was a lot more downs than ups. I've just had to work really, really hard to get to where I'm at," he said.

"I've just kept working my butt off trying to be great. I want to be as great as possible. I want to be the greatest. I want to be the best in my position."

articles.title: Would the Colts make the NFL playoffs if the season ended today?
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are in a five-way tie for the seventh and final playoff berth in the AFC. Here's a look at their odds to make the playoffs
articles.body:
No, the Indianapolis Colts would not be in the playoff if the season ended today. At 2-2, they are tied with four other teams for the seventh and final berth. Here's the seeding:

7. New England: Wins tiebreaker due to 2-1 conference record

8. Denver: Gets the 8 seed due to 1-1 conference record

9. Pittsburgh: Division tiebreakers are determined first so Cincinnati is eliminated due to head-to-head; the Steelers have the strength of victory tiebreaker over Colts

Indianapolis Colts vs Washington Commanders photos in NFL Week 4 action

NFL.com gives the Colts a 39% chance of making the playoffs, 9th best in the AFC. Playoffstatus.com has them at 45%, 10th-best odds in the AFC.

Obviously, Sunday's game against the Steelers is potentially a big one for playoff seeding.

The Colts are also one-game out of the AFC South with two games to play against the Jaguars .

It's way too early to focus on tiebreakers but the Colts have legitimate playoff hopes (for now).

Joel A. Erickson and Nathan Brown cover the Colts all season. Get more coverage on IndyStarTV and with the Colts Insider newsletter .

articles.title: Week 5 NFL power rankings: Where Indianapolis Colts rank among 2-2 teams
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts improve their record, but that doesn't necessarily equate to a boost in the NFL power rankings.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are one of 11 NFL teams with a 2-2 record, but are "average" squads made the same?

They posted a 17-point win in Week 4 , their largest since Week 8 of last season. That's impressive, right?

The NFL power rankings aren't convinced, placing the Colts low among .500 teams.

NFL power rankings: Indianapolis Colts rank poorly among 2-2 teams

The Athletic : 19th, unchanged from last week, 8th among 2-2 teams

"The Colts went to London and didn't have to do much to beat up on the undermanned Washington Commanders . But there's rising concern about Daniel Jones, who completed 19-of-34 passes for just 143 yards with no touchdowns and an interception in his return from an Achilles injury."

Aaron Leming, SB Nation : 23rd, last among 2-2 teams

"Following an 0-2 start, the Colts have fought their way back to .500. While that might look good on paper, the quality of those two wins is questionable at best. This team has far too much money tied up in key positions at quarterback and on defense, and it hasn't gotten the desired return thus far. That might be the key to getting this season back on track and back into the playoffs."

Frank Schwab, Yahoo : 22nd, down 3, 10th among 2-2 teams

"Injuries at receiver have been an issue. Missing Alec Pierce changes how defenses approach the Colts, without the threat of big plays downfield. Still, Daniel Jones looks much worse than he did last season, and it's fair to wonder if his Achilles tear plays a part in that. He still has the support of Colts coach Shane Steichen, who said Jones is doing a good job."

Vinnie Iyer, Sporting News : 23rd, up 1, last among 2-2 teams

"The Colts needed some schedule breaks after facing the Ravens and Chiefs to open the season. They got them from the Texans and Commanders with Jonathan Taylor and the defense making it easier on Daniel Jones. Getting the Steelers and Titans next can keep Indy hot."

Indianapolis Colts vs Washington Commanders photos in NFL Week 4 action

Pete Prisco, CBS Sports : 22nd, down 2, 10th among 2-2 teams

"At 2-2, they have righted things after opening 0-2. They wised up in the victory over the Commanders and gave the ball to Jonathan Taylor."

Brent Sobleski, Bleacher Report : 23rd, unchanged, last among 2-2 teams

"Shane Steichen's squad isn't close to where it was before last season's second-half collapse. Quarterback Daniel Jones was a huge part of that early success. He's been part of the problem to start this season despite the two-game winning streak."

Nate Davis, USA TODAY : 23rd, up 1, 10th among 2-2 teams

"Maybe they should pack the Mayflower trucks (ships?) for Europe given they've won three in a row in the Old World, which the NFL seems ready to make its new frontier."

Mike Florio, Pro Football Talk : 22nd, up 2, 10th among 2-2 teams

"Can they win enough games to steal a wild-card berth?"

Conor Orr, Sports Illustrated : 17th, down 2, 6th among 2-2 teams

"I don't really care what happens to this iteration of the Colts, but following the Sauce Gardner trade last year, literally the only sensible follow-up is to continue pouring resources into this team and trading for Colts legacy son Marvin Harrison Jr."

articles.title: NY Giants fans think Odell Beckham Jr. call aged poorly as replacement gets season-ending surgery
articles.summary: The New York Giants released Odell Beckham Jr. after just a few games, hoping Braxton Berrios could replace him.
articles.body:
The New York Giants released Odell Beckham Jr. after just a few games, hoping Braxton Berrios could replace him.

However, Berrios, who was signed to the Giants' practice squad after Beckham was released, is now set to undergo season-ending surgery.

This leaves the Giants light on depth at the WR position, especially after releasing Beckham. And fans are concerned the franchise may have made a mistake.

New York Giants fans believe team cut Odell Beckham Jr. 'for nothing' after Braxton Berrios injury

Against the Arizona Cardinals, New York Giants WR Braxton Berrios suffered a foot injury that forced him out of the game early on.

The injury appears to be worse than initially thought, as Berrios has undergone season-ending foot surgery to address the issue.

Understandably, Giants fans and NFL fans as a whole pointed out how much this decision looks even worse in the aftermath of the franchise releasing Odell Beckham Jr.

One fan simply wrote, "Giants should've treated my boy right," while another fan added, "So they cut Odell for nothing."

A third fan pointed to the timeline of the situation to highlight the comedy of errors, noting, "They cut OBJ, signed Berrios, and now Berrios is done for the season. Great work, guys."

"Giants have a plague with injuries this season that I've never seen before. Oh my days," wrote a fourth fan, pointing to the other high-profile injuries to players like Jaxson Dart along with Berrios.

A fifth fan suggested the Giants might reach out to Beckham Jr., noting, "That call to OBJ gonna be so awkward."

"They let go of OBJ for this guy, and he gets hurt on the first start? WTH is going on in the NFL? I know OBJ is thinking what I'm thinking," joked a sixth fan, trying to suggest Beckham Jr. was happy with this situation.

And lastly, one fan shut down any notion of Beckham Jr. being brought back, saying, "Peeps saying sign OBJ. Dude is old and washed. You don't win games by aura farming."

Even with this injury to Berrios, it is highly unlikely that the Giants will bring back Odell Beckham Jr., given that the release seemed to cause a permanent rift in their relationship.
